newsitem.title: USA: Web measurement, audit firms form marketing pact.
newsitem.headline: Web measurement, audit firms form marketing pact.

text.p: NetCount LLC and BPA International executives said they had formed a marketing alliance aimed at expanding adoption of standards for advertising over the World Wide Web.

Paul Grand, founder and chairman of NetCount, said in an interview the alliance, which will include a certification of the NetCount/Price Waterhouse Web measurement products and a U.S. education program, aimed to "get rid of the confusion" surrounding advertising on the Internet.

Grand said independent research organizations predicted the Web advertising market would grow to $5 billion by the end of the decade, and could reach as much as $1 billion this year compared to about $300 million in 1996.
NetCount conducts measurement for around 435 Web sites, and BPA has conducted audits for more than 30 Web sites.

Peter Black, senior vice-president of BPA, said the alliance aimed to "position our companies as pioneers and market leaders" by emphasizing the speculation between the roles of advertising accountancy and auditing.
"There's no mutual investment and we don't have a revenue sharing arrangement," said Grand. (sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
